newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bushfires may burn into next week.
newsitem.headline: Australian bushfires may burn into next week.

text.p: Australia's bushfire season has arrived with more than 100 fires in three states destroying more than 100,000 hectares (250,000 acres) and some fires could burn into next week, fire officials said on Monday.
But forecast searing temperatures failed to materialise on Monday, allowing thousands of fire fighters to gain control of most fires.
"We have escaped it today," said New South Wales state bushfire commissioner Phil Koperberg.
"We were faced with 30 major fires today and they are either under control or are in the process of being brought under control," Koperberg told reporters.
At one stage a bushfire broke out on the foreshore of Sydney Harbour at Dobroyd Head, burning some two hectares (five acres), but was brought under control without any damage to property.
In January 1994 hundreds of bushfires raged across eastern Australia, with fires ringing Sydney, dropping ash on beaches, burning homes and killing four people.
Fires burning in the northeast New South Wales for the past few days have burnt some 9,740 hectares (24,000 acres), with eight still out of control, a bushfire spokesman told Reuters.
In the state of Queensland fires have destroyed at 100,000 hectares of scrub in the state's southeast, with the largest fire near Chinchilla, 160 km (99 miles) northwest of Brisbane.

"This fire is not contained and the danger is that it may join up with two others," said Judith Mishinski, spokeswoman for the Queensland Fire Service. Other fires were only 30 km (19 miles) from the state capital Brisbane.
Queensland fire inspector Alan Johnson said forecast showers were the best hope of containing the outbreaks which have burned for three days and could burn into next week.
In the state of South Australia fire fighters managed to control some 80 fires, most in bush and pastoral land.

The largest remaining fire, sparked by a lightning strike, had burnt 20,000 hectares (49,500 acres) of the Flinders Range. Fire officials in the three states said the fires had not damaged any urban areas or caused any injuries.
Total fire bans have been imposed in the three states with temperatures reaching the mid-30s Celsius (86 Fahrenheit) and winds gusting up to 60 kph (37 mph).

Australia's bushfire seasons normally runs during the summer months of December to February, but can be longer as the island continent often suffers severe droughts leaving much of the country tinder-dry.
